explanation: Within the taxonomic hierarchy, higher categories are more inclusive; organisms grouped in the same domain share only general traits, whereas members of a species share highly specific characteristics. While taxonomists traditionally relied on anatomical data to classify organisms, modern classification is aided by DNA barcoding. This technology compares short fragments of DNA from an unknown organism against a database of known sequences. The Consortium for the Barcode of Life (CBOL) proposes that scientists will be able to instantly identify species using handheld scanners, treating DNA as the universal product code (UPC) of life. This barcoding system offers a rapid, inexpensive method for cataloging biodiversity.

questions.exp: DNA barcoding is the identification of species by comparing short fragments of their DNA sequences to a reference database of known organisms.
